assumptions.condition: For every \(n\), \(\{X_t:t\in\mathbb Z\}\) is strictly stationary under \(P_n\).

standard.name: strict stationarity for long-panel time-series inference

assumptions.condition: The absolute-regularity coefficients satisfy \(\beta_n(j)\leq C_{\beta}\exp(-c_{\beta}j)\) for every \(j\geq1\) and every \(n\).
The primitive process obeys \(\sup_n\mathbb E_n\lVert X_t\rVert^{8+\delta_0}\leq C_{\mathrm{mom}}\).

standard.name: uniform fixed high-moment condition for dependent GMM
comparable long pre- and post-treatment horizons
square proximal bridge full-rank condition with a fixed margin
valid proximal synthetic-control bridge for each predeclared role

assumptions.condition: The population criterion difference satisfies \(\sqrt n(L_1-L_2)\to d\in\mathbb R\).
The long-run covariance matrix of \((\ell_{1,t}-L_1,\ell_{2,t}-L_2,\psi_{1,t},\psi_{2,t},v_{1,t},v_{2,t})\) converges to a finite positive-semidefinite matrix.

standard.name: fixed positive marginal asymptotic-variance condition for studentized GMM

assumptions.condition: For the fixed finite envelope \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}\), the whole triangular array satisfies \(\sup_{n\geq1}|\sqrt n(L_{1,n}-L_{2,n})|\leq D_{\mathrm{gap}}\).

standard.name: nondegenerate local selection statistic with a fixed margin

definitions.name: same-pre-period ridge role selector
definitions.construction: Compute \(\widehat L_s=\min_a n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^n\{Y_t-W_{D_s,t}^{\prime}a\}^2+\lVert a\rVert_2^2\) for \(s\in\{1,2\}\), and set \(\widehat J=1\) when \(\widehat L_1\leq\widehat L_2\) and \(\widehat J=2\) otherwise.

definitions.name: conventional role-selected proximal ATT
definitions.construction: For each role, compute \(\widehat M_s\), \(\widehat\mu_s^{\mathrm{post}}\), \(\widehat H_s\), the fitted scores \(\widehat\psi_{s,t}\) and \(\widehat v_{s,t}\), their centered sample autocovariances through \(q_n=\lfloor\min(n,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\), and the Bartlett estimates \(\widehat\Omega_{\psi,s}\) and \(\widehat\Omega_{v,s}\). Set \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}=\widehat\tau_{\widehat J}\), \(\widehat{\operatorname{se}}^{\mathrm{conv}}_s=\{\widehat\Omega_{\psi,s}/n+\widehat\Omega_{v,s}/m\}^{1/2}\), and report \([\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}\pm z\widehat{\operatorname{se}}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{\widehat J}]\). This construction uses the full pre-period sample both to select the role and to fit its bridge, unlike \(\text{def:gap-split-estimator}\).

definitions.name: binary selected-Gaussian coverage functional
definitions.construction: \(C_z(k)=\int_{-\infty}^{k}\phi(x)g_{\rho_1}(x;z)\,dx+\int_k^{\infty}\phi(x)g_{\rho_2}(x;z)\,dx\), where \(g_{\rho}\) is the conditional probability that a standard normal coordinate correlated by \(\rho\) with \(X=x\) lies in \([-z,z]\).

definitions.name: primitive Gaussian proximal family
definitions.construction: For \(\theta=(\mu,f,b,x,y,\zeta,r,t_1,t_2)\in\Theta_{\mathcal G}^{\mathrm{leg}}\) and \(d\in\mathbb R\), set \(B=\mu^2+f\), \(R=t_1+B+x\), \(\eta=B/R\), \(K=\mu/B\), \(c_1=t_1^{-1/2}\), \(t_{2,n}=t_2-(R^2/B^2)d/\sqrt n\), and \(c_{2,n}=t_{2,n}^{-1/2}\). Generate independent Gaussian coordinates \(F_t\sim N(\mu,f)\), \(e_{0t}\sim N(0,b)\), \(e_{1t}\sim N(0,x)\), \(e_{2t}\sim N(0,y)\), and \(\xi_t\sim N(0,\zeta)\); put \(Y_t(0)=F_t+e_{0t}\), \(\Delta_t=\tau+\xi_t\), \(W_{1t}=c_1(F_t+e_{1t})\), and \(W_{2t}=c_{2,n}(F_t+e_{2t})\), with the two roles exchanging donor and proxy positions. The legal tied manifold has \(t_2=t_1+x-y>0\); along the local calibration, \(t_{2,n}>0\) eventually, both bridge matrices equal \(c_1c_{2,n}B\), the bridge coefficients are \(1/c_1\) and \(1/c_{2,n}\), and \(\sqrt n(L_1-L_2)=d+O(n^{-1/2})\). At the tied limit, \(\sigma_D^2=4\eta^2\{(1-\eta)^2B+b\}(x+y)+2\eta^4(x^2+y^2)\), \(c_{D1}=\operatorname{Cov}(D,A_1)=-2\eta K\{(1-\eta)Bx+by\}\), \(c_{D2}=\operatorname{Cov}(D,A_2)=2\eta K\{(1-\eta)By+bx\}\), \(V_1=K^2(B+y)(b+x)+r(b+x+\zeta)\), and \(V_2=K^2(B+x)(b+y)+r(b+y+\zeta)\). Hence the continuous map is \(\Gamma(\theta,d)=(-d/\sigma_D,c_{D1}/\sqrt{\sigma_D^2V_1},c_{D2}/\sqrt{\sigma_D^2V_2},V_1,V_2)\). The family \(\mathcal G\) is the collection of these local Gaussian arrays.

definitions.name: early-select, late-fit proximal ATT
definitions.construction: Select \(\widehat J_A\) by the ridge rule on \(\mathcal F_A\); discard \(\lceil(\log n)^2\rceil\) observations; solve the selected bridge moment on \(\mathcal B_n\); average the selected fitted residual on \(\mathcal C_n\); and studentize using separate Bartlett HAC estimates on \(\mathcal B_n\) and \(\mathcal C_n\) with bandwidth \(h_n\).

definitions.name: singular joint Gaussian and HAC mapping handle
definitions.construction: Couple logarithmically separated beta-mixing big blocks to independent blocks, prove Cramér--Wold approximation along covariance-convergent subsequences, control Gaussian selector-boundary strips using only \(\operatorname{Var}(D)\geq\nu\), and studentize each selected ATT direction using its own positive scalar variance rather than inverting the stacked covariance.

statements.justification: This expansion exposes the two role-specific ATT coordinates that the ridge selector switches between.
statements.gap: Shi et al. and Qiu et al. linearize a predetermined proximal role; the simultaneous two-role expansion must also retain the loss coordinates driving selection.
statements.consumer: It supplies the joint influence array used by both the conventional coverage diagnostic and the separated correction.

statements.statement: For each \(s\in\mathcal S\), under \(q_n=\lfloor\min(n,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\), replacement of \(M_s\), \(\mu_s\), \(\alpha_s\), and \(\tau\) by \(\widehat M_s\), \(\widehat\mu_s^{\mathrm{post}}\), \(\widehat\alpha_s\), and \(\widehat\tau_s\) in the fitted influence scores is asymptotically negligible for Bartlett estimation: \(\widehat\Omega_{\psi,s}\to_{P_n}\Omega_{\psi,s}\), \(\widehat\Omega_{v,s}\to_{P_n}\Omega_{v,s}\), and \(\widehat V_s^{\mathrm{conv}}\to_{P_n}V_s\). Moreover, \(\Pr_{P_n}\{\min_{s\in\mathcal S}\widehat V_s^{\mathrm{conv}}\geq\nu/2\}\to1\).
statements.justification: This lemma certifies that the concrete same-sample Bartlett standard error consistently studentizes each role coordinate without requiring inversion of the stacked covariance.
statements.gap: Andrews gives kernel HAC consistency for observed score arrays, while the conventional proximal interval requires uniform control of fitted bridge-Jacobian and ATT replacement in two role-specific score arrays.
statements.consumer: It makes the conventional selected-Gaussian coverage functional operational from the observed panel.

statements.statement: Let \((Q_1,Q_2,A_1,A_2)\) be the centered Gaussian limit of the pre-period loss and ATT coordinates, and let \((R_1,R_2)\) be the centered Gaussian post-period limit, independent of the pre-period limit. For each \(s\in\mathcal S\), the fitted-score Bartlett estimator with \(q_n=\lfloor\min(n,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\) satisfies \(\widehat V_s^{\mathrm{conv}}\to_{P_n}V_s\) and \(\Pr_{P_n}\{\widehat V_s^{\mathrm{conv}}>0\}\to1\). Consequently, \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}-\tau)\Rightarrow A_{J(d)}+\sqrt rR_{J(d)}\), and \((\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}-\tau)/\widehat{\operatorname{se}}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{\widehat J}\Rightarrow T_1\mathbf 1\{X\leq k\}+T_2\mathbf 1\{X>k\}\). This strictly extends the fixed-role limit of Shi et al. (2026) to the nonregular local role-selection boundary while reducing to that result when \(|d|\to\infty\).
statements.justification: The theorem identifies the actual first-order law reported after outcome-based donor/proxy role choice.
statements.gap: Shi et al. derive normality only for a predetermined role, while Lee et al. target a conditional selective pivot rather than this switched causal coordinate.
statements.consumer: An analyst comparing two scientifically credible West-German role assignments can calculate the asymptotic law of the reported conventional proximal ATT.

statements.statement: For every \(z>0\), the limiting coverage of the conventional selected interval is \(C_z(k)\). At an exact selector tie, \(C_z(0)=2\Phi(z)-1\) for all \(\rho_1,\rho_2\in[-1,1]\). For any fixed \(z>0\), \(C_z(k)=2\Phi(z)-1\) for every \(k\in\mathbb R\) if and only if \(\rho_1^2=\rho_2^2\). If \(k\neq0\) and \(\rho_1^2\neq\rho_2^2\), then \(\operatorname{sign}\{C_z(k)-[2\Phi(z)-1]\}=\operatorname{sign}\{k(\rho_1^2-\rho_2^2)\}\).
statements.justification: The coverage function separates harmless selected asymmetry from genuine two-sided Wald distortion and gives its strict direction.
statements.gap: Leeb, Pötscher, and Ewald give comparator-specific Gaussian coverage formulas, and Azzalini--Regoli give even-functional symmetry; neither gives this selected-coordinate all-gap if-and-only-if boundary.
statements.consumer: The equality \(\rho_1^2=\rho_2^2\) is a feasible robustness diagnostic for deciding whether conventional role-selected intervals require correction.

statements.statement: Equip \(\Theta_{\mathcal G}^{\mathrm{leg}}\) with the Euclidean topology relative to \(t_2=t_1+x-y\) and its strict bridge-rank, moment, selector-variance, and ATT-variance inequalities. For any fixed \(\kappa<2\), \(\nu<13/40\), and \(C_{\mathrm{mom}}\) exceeding the \(8+\delta_0\) Gaussian moments at the displayed points, the symmetric point \(\theta=(1,1,1,1,1,1,r,1,1)\), for any fixed \(r>0\), is legal and has \(\rho_1=-\rho_2\), a nonzero selected limiting mean, and exact symmetric coverage for every local gap. At the asymmetric legal point \(\theta=(1,1,1/10,1/5,9/5,1/10,1/10,9/5,1/5)\), the primitive formulas give \(B=2\), \(R=4\), \(\eta=K=1/2\), \(\sigma_D^2=161/100\), \(c_{D1}=-19/100\), \(c_{D2}=91/100\), \(V_1=13/40\), and \(V_2=249/200\), so \(\rho_1=-0.262663049718703\) and \(\rho_2=0.6427525060282437\). With \(d/\sigma_D=-1\), equivalently \(k=1\), and \(z=\Phi^{-1}(0.95)\), substitution in \(C_z(k)\) gives \(C_z(1)=0.8858209104904335\) to the displayed numerical precision. The local scale \(t_{2,n}=t_2-(R^2/B^2)d/\sqrt n=1/5-4d/\sqrt n\) realizes that drift while preserving both bridge equalities and every strict legality margin eventually. Continuity of \(\Gamma(\theta,d)=(k,\rho_1,\rho_2,V_1,V_2)\), positivity at that asymmetric point, and the strict inequality \(\rho_1^2<\rho_2^2\) yield a relatively open neighborhood of legal local arrays with strict undercoverage; exchanging the role labels yields the opposite strict squared-correlation ordering, while reversing the drift sign yields strict overcoverage.
statements.justification: Primitive realization prevents the Gaussian frontier from being an unattainable covariance thought experiment.
statements.gap: Generic post-selection examples do not verify simultaneous proximal bridge validity, ridge-loss calibration, and positive ATT and selector variances inside a panel law.
statements.consumer: The asymmetric family provides a calibrated stress test for a two-role proximal synthetic-control implementation.

statements.justification: The corrected estimator needs no additional primitive variance assumption beyond the conventional fixed-role marginal margin.
statements.gap: Scalar HAC positivity for the retained blocks is inherited algebraically here rather than imposed as a separate condition.
statements.consumer: It licenses coordinate-wise studentization of either early-selected role in the uniform split-sample question.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}<\infty\), can the singular joint Gaussian and HAC mapping handle establish \(\sup_{(P_j)_{j\geq1}\in\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})}\mathbb E_{P_n}[\sup_x|\Pr_{P_n}\{(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau)/\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\widehat J_A}\leq x\mid\mathcal F_A\}-\Phi(x)|]\to0\), where the supremum ranges over whole triangular arrays satisfying \(\sup_{j\geq1}|\sqrt j(L_{1,j}-L_{2,j})|\leq D_{\mathrm{gap}}\), the stacked long-run covariance may be positive semidefinite, \(\operatorname{Var}(D)\geq\nu\), and \(V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}\geq V_s\geq\nu\) for both roles?
statements.justification: This is the unresolved theorem-assembly bottleneck needed for a practical correction that remains valid at local role ties and singular joint covariances.
statements.gap: Lunde supplies separated-block distributional transfer and Andrews supplies HAC consistency, but neither composes proximal inverse estimation, fitted-score replacement, scalar studentization, and discontinuous role selection uniformly on this covariance class.
statements.consumer: A positive answer yields selector-conditional Wald inference for a predeclared two-role robustness redesign without estimating the non-identifiable local loss drift.

statements.statement: If one role is fixed in advance, or if \(|d|\to\infty\) so that one role is selected with probability tending to one, the selected limit and its symmetric-Wald coverage reduce to the fixed-role normal and nominal-coverage result; the gap-split estimator reduces as a construction to fixed-role late-block proximal inference, with its declared sample-splitting variance rather than the full-pre-period efficiency bound.
statements.justification: The reduction verifies compatibility with the published predetermined-role theory and makes the efficiency cost of splitting explicit.
statements.gap: The reduction is a required sanity check rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It lets applied users interpret the correction as ordinary fixed-role proximal inference away from the selection boundary.

sampling_model.design: Observational long-panel sampling with two predeclared square donor/proxy partitions and deterministic treatment onset after period \(n\).
sampling_model.units: One treated unit and a fixed-dimensional vector of untreated controls observed for \(n+m\) periods.
sampling_model.treatment: The treated outcome equals \(Y_t(0)\) before onset and \(Y_t(0)+\Delta_t\) afterward; controls remain untreated.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; identification is through two valid proximal bridge systems with fixed singular-value margin.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each bridge is estimated from pre-treatment moments. The conventional procedure uses all \(n\) pre-period observations for both selection and bridge fitting, replaces the bridge Jacobian, post donor mean, bridge coefficient, and ATT in its influence scores, and uses separate pre- and post-period Bartlett estimates with \(q_n=\lfloor\min(n,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\). The correction instead selects early, discards a logarithm-squared gap, fits late, averages post residuals, and uses Bartlett bandwidth \(h_n=\lfloor\min(|\mathcal B_n|,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For a predetermined donor/proxy partition, the proximal bridge moment identifies the synthetic-control weights and fixed-role GMM/HAC inference is asymptotically normal.
Conditioning a Gaussian linear statistic on a polyhedral selection event yields an exact truncated-normal pivot and conditional confidence interval.
Explicit Gaussian formulas characterize coverage of naive and protected intervals after selection between two nested regression models.
Even functionals are invariant under the paper's skew-symmetric perturbation construction.
Separated-block sample splitting is asymptotically valid for broad beta-mixing time-series functionals under stability conditions.
Kernel long-run covariance estimators are consistent under serial dependence and suitable bandwidth growth.
Section 5, Theorem 3 establishes asymptotic normality of the article's doubly robust GMM estimator when at least one of its two bridge models is correctly specified.
For a fixed proximal proxy structure, influence functions, semiparametric efficiency bounds, and locally efficient estimators are characterized.
Simultaneous protection over all candidate submodels guarantees post-selection coverage under arbitrary selection rules.

tldr: Two valid proximal synthetic-control role assignments can identify the same ATT yet produce a nonregular conventional interval when the role with smaller pre-period ridge loss is reported. The same-sample conventional interval is fully specified by fitted bridge and post-residual influence scores and separate Bartlett long-run variance estimates with bandwidth \(q_n=\lfloor\min(n,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\). The project derives its selected-Gaussian law and exact coverage function, proves that every exact selector tie preserves every symmetric Wald level, establishes all-gap validity exactly when the two standardized ATT coordinates have equal squared correlations with the loss contrast, and signs strict miscoverage otherwise. A finite-dimensional primitive Gaussian chart realizes both regimes; its explicit asymmetric point has limiting coverage \(0.8858209104904335\) for a nominal \(90\%\) interval, and strict miscoverage persists in the chart's Euclidean relative topology. The distinct correction separates early role selection from late bridge fitting and post residual averaging; its remaining open theorem asks for uniform selector-conditional Bartlett-studentized normality over whole triangular arrays with a fixed finite root-\(n\) loss-gap envelope and singular joint covariances.

project_justification.gap: Published proximal synthetic-control theory predetermines donor and proxy roles, while general selective-inference theory does not characterize unconditional conventional symmetric-Wald coverage for a statistic that changes coordinates with the selected role.
project_justification.niche: The binary ridge selector has enough Gaussian geometry for an exact if-and-only-if coverage frontier, yet its covariance coordinates retain a substantive proximal interpretation through bridge Jacobians, donor means, and long-run residual variation.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the selected limit, the evaluable coverage map, the squared-correlation frontier and strict sign rule, a continuous finite-dimensional primitive realization map, and a separated estimator whose uniform singular-covariance mapping over bounded-gap triangular arrays is exposed as the first-class open question.

related_work: Shi et al. (2026) provide the writing and causal setup exemplar: excluded controls serve as supplemental proxies, fixed bridge moments identify a synthetic-control ATT, and long-panel GMM uses HAC inference. The present theorem changes the first post-linearization step by allowing two predeclared valid roles to be selected with the same observations. Lee et al. (2016) supply the Gaussian half-space conditioning technique, but their target is an exact conditional selective pivot. Leeb, Pötscher, and Ewald (2015) demonstrate that explicit post-selection coverage calculations are possible for nested regression models; their selector and reported target differ from the proximal switched-coordinate functional here. Azzalini and Regoli (2012) explain the even-function symmetry behind exact tie protection, so symmetry alone is not claimed as new. Lunde (2019) supplies the separated-block beta-mixing transfer, and Andrews (1991) supplies Bartlett-HAC control; both are supporting methods for the corrected estimator. Section 5, Theorem 3 of Qiu et al. (2024) gives asymptotic normality for the article's doubly robust GMM estimator when at least one of its two bridge models is correctly specified; it is fixed-role machinery rather than a role-selection result. Cui et al. (2024) provide fixed-proxy proximal influence-function and efficiency theory. Berk et al. (2013) give universally protected simultaneous intervals, whereas the present target is the exact frontier on which the ordinary role-specific critical value already works.
technical_internal_limitation: The Gaussian coverage algebra and the finite-dimensional primitive covariance map have direct calculations, but the publication-level uniform joint Gaussian/HAC mapping over singular stacked covariances remains open. The required proof must avoid full covariance inversion, handle row-dependent positive-semidefinite limits over the whole-array class \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\), and control the discontinuous selector by its one-dimensional positive variance margin. The reported decimal is reproducible quadrature of the exact formula; strict undercoverage follows from the analytic sign theorem rather than a certified numerical error bound.
honest_scope: The theorem concerns exactly two predeclared square bridge systems, ridge penalty one, stationary geometrically beta-mixing panels, fixed moment and rank radii, and positive ATT and selector-contrast variance margins. The split-sample variance margin is not separately assumed: \(V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}\geq V_s\geq\nu\) follows from its definition. The conventional interval uses the full pre-period sample for both selection and bridge fitting and uses its own fitted-score Bartlett standard error with bandwidth \(q_n=\lfloor\min(n,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\); it is distinct from the early-select, gap-separated correction. The open correction is posed for each fixed finite \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}\) over whole arrays in \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\), not over unrelated per-row laws. The analysis does not cover the actual rectangular, simplex-constrained six-donor and ten-proxy rule used in the published West-German application, estimate the local population loss drift, recover full-pre-period efficiency after splitting, or solve the three-or-more-role cone problem. The exact-tie symmetry mechanism, generic sample splitting, and Bartlett HAC are established ingredients. The new claim is their proximal selected-coordinate coverage frontier and primitive realization. Under a fixed role or a diverging loss gap, the construction reduces to published fixed-role proximal normality; this is a sanity reduction, not a contribution.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The preprint was read at the Introduction, Assumption 4 and Theorem 2, Theorem 3, the West-German application, and the Discussion. The paper fixes donor and supplemental-proxy roles before its bridge moment and HAC limit are formed.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive the selected-coordinate Gaussian limit and the exact unconditional symmetric-Wald coverage function when two valid square roles are selected by the smaller same-pre-period ridge loss.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed-role smooth GMM map after the bridge expansion by a discontinuous Gaussian half-space map that selects one of two correlated ATT coordinates.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining proximal synthetic control, donor or proxy role selection, local loss ties, conventional Wald coverage, and squared selector correlations found fixed-role proximal inference and generic post-selection theory, but no exact target--method pair.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is immediate from Lee et al. because the selector is a Gaussian half-space. Rebuttal: their result conditions to construct a selective pivot; it neither computes unconditional coverage of a conventional interval that switches coordinates nor derives the all-gap squared-correlation frontier or realizes it within legal proximal panels.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The focal object is the evaluable coverage function \(C_z(k)\); the seed includes an exact if-and-only-if boundary, a strict sign law, a primitive open family, and a correction rather than a generic warning about selection.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Definition 1, Theorem 1 and its coupling proof, the dependent central-limit argument, and the closing proof section were read. The paper proves general separated-block validity but leaves inference for the second block to the target-specific analysis.
seed_details.opportunity: Prove selector-conditional studentized normality for early role choice, a logarithm-squared gap, late bridge fitting, post residual averaging, and Bartlett HAC uniformly over whole triangular arrays with a fixed finite root-\(n\) loss-gap envelope and singular stacked covariance.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace full covariance whitening by scalar studentization in the two nondegenerate ATT directions and selector-boundary anti-concentration in the one nondegenerate contrast direction.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination pair of beta-mixing sample splitting and proximal-GMM studentization under singular joint covariance was not occupied; Lunde supplies the separation transfer and Andrews supplies HAC control separately.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: sample splitting under beta mixing is already Lunde's theorem. Rebuttal: that theorem is supporting machinery; the remaining result is the uniform proximal inverse, fitted-score HAC, and singular selected mapping needed for conditional studentization.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed does not claim generic splitting as novelty and makes the singular-covariance uniform mapping the named open content.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The abstract, simultaneous-inference construction, asymptotic protection result, and concluding comparison were read. The construction protects arbitrary selection by widening all candidate intervals rather than characterizing when the unadjusted selected interval is exact.
seed_details.opportunity: For at least three valid roles, derive the Gaussian cone-integral coverage function and an if-and-only-if covariance geometry for nominal coverage at every local loss-gap vector.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace binary half-line integration by integration over the normal fan of the minimum-loss polyhedron, including singular faces and unequal ATT variances.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing multi-role proximal synthetic control with Gaussian cones and conventional Wald exactness returned PoSI and polyhedral conditional pivots, but no all-gap role-specific coverage characterization.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: PoSI already solves arbitrary role selection. Rebuttal: PoSI gives conservative simultaneous protection; this seed asks for the exact geometry under which no widening is needed and a proximal-dependent correction when it is.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed has a named cone-coverage functional and an if-and-only-if target; feasibility is lower because the binary squared-correlation boundary need not generalize cleanly.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, proximal identification results, Theorem 3.1 efficiency calculation, and Discussion were read. The efficiency bound is derived for a fixed proxy structure and does not optimize over donor--proxy allocations.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the partition minimizing the long-run proximal-ATT influence variance and construct inference that is uniform at local variance ties.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed tangent-space projection by a finite family of role-specific influence functions before optimizing their long-run variances.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for efficiency-optimal donor--proxy allocation found fixed-structure proximal efficiency and minimal bridge regularization, but no optimization across role assignments.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: choose the role with the smallest estimated HAC variance and split the sample. Rebuttal: that recipe does not characterize the population optimum or give uniform risk and coverage at local variance ties.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The frontier would have to be derived from role-specific influence functions; until that derivation is available this ranks below the directly verified loss-selection kernel.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorem 1 identification condition, majority-validity corollary, adaptive-LASSO construction, oracle-limit result, and concluding discussion were read. Its setting is an independent point-exposure system with sparse invalid proxies.
seed_details.opportunity: Bound the proximal synthetic-control ATT under role-specific exclusion violations, derive a critical violation radius at which zero enters, and obtain selection-robust endpoint inference.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace sparse validity selection by a sharp optimization over bounded perturbations of two serially dependent bridge systems.
seed_details.destination_search: The bounded-violation, time-series bridge, and role-selection combination was not located; nearby work either selects invalid point-treatment proxies or bounds donor spillover bias.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: invalid-proxy sensitivity is an immediate norm bound on moment error. Rebuttal: swapping roles changes the inverse bridge operator and the sharp joint endpoint problem; the critical radius and post-selection uniform inference are not supplied by a triangle inequality.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed requires closed or algorithmically sharp endpoints and a named critical radius; absent those it would be rejected as sufficient-only sensitivity.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The cited mathematical review finding was opened. It records that post-transport makes the displayed spectral object causal while target-pre-span is unused in the reviewed proof.
seed_details.opportunity: Give a necessary-and-sufficient characterization of when target-pre-span substitutes for post-transport in spectral or proximal panel identification.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Redo the causal interpretation of the spectral bridge after deleting post-transport and derive either an implication from span or a pair of legal counterexamples.
seed_details.destination_search: Bridge-equivalence work was located, but the precise span-versus-transport logical frontier was not found in the accessible panel literature.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is only assumption pruning in one proof. Rebuttal: it survives only if the necessity direction yields a reusable identification frontier across the published bridge class; otherwise the seed should be dropped.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The source is a prior-proposal proof boundary rather than published prior art, so evidence and consumer value are weaker.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, polyhedral lemma, Theorems 5.3 and 6.1, proof by truncated-normal conditioning, and Discussion were read. The target there is a fixed selected regression coefficient under a Gaussian model.
seed_details.opportunity: Construct a feasible conditional pivot for the same-sample role-selected proximal ATT using an estimated long-run joint Gaussian law, avoiding the efficiency loss of time splitting.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a known finite-sample Gaussian covariance and affine response by a dependent asymptotic influence representation with estimated HAC covariance and a changing target coordinate.
seed_details.destination_search: No proximal time-series selective pivot with estimated long-run covariance was found, but generic selective central-limit theory makes novelty vulnerable.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: plug the joint HAC covariance into Lee et al.'s truncated-normal pivot. Rebuttal: uniform validity near singular covariance and estimated selection boundaries is not automatic, but the generic selective-inference literature may subsume much of the needed step.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped from the top set because its novelty rebuttal is less secure than the unconditional Wald frontier.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Assumption 4 and Theorem 2, Theorem 3, application, and Discussion were read. Its fixed-role HAC construction leaves open how a finite menu should be protected after pre-period fit selection; Leeb, Pötscher, and Ewald was then read as adjacent method literature.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive the least common critical value protecting a finite proximal-role menu uniformly over local loss gaps and characterize its excess length relative to the binary symmetry frontier.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace nested-model coefficient geometry by a selected family of correlated proximal-ATT influence coordinates and optimize the Gaussian critical value over local gaps.
seed_details.destination_search: PoSI already gives universal protection, and no evidence was found that the role-specific least critical value has a sufficiently new closed form.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is a two-coordinate PoSI constant. Rebuttal: a role-specific local-gap optimum could be sharper, but without a closed-form frontier the objection largely holds.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Assumption 4 and Theorem 2, Theorem 3, application, and Discussion were read. Its application uses an overidentified practical role allocation, and Qiu et al. was then read as the adjacent fixed-role GMM method exemplar.
seed_details.opportunity: Generalize the role-selection coverage analysis to overidentified rectangular GMM systems and simplex-constrained donor weights resembling the German application.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the square inverse bridge expansion by a constrained or overidentified GMM directional derivative whose active set can itself change with the selector.
seed_details.destination_search: Fixed-role overidentified proximal GMM is occupied, while selection over role assignments and active simplex faces was not found.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is a routine square-to-rectangular extension. Rebuttal: simplex active-set changes create an additional nonregular layer, but that layer also makes the kernel substantially less feasible than the square binary theorem.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Not selected because a routine rectangular extension would fail the novelty bar and a genuine active-set treatment is too broad for the first version.

literature_map.chosen_kernel: Shi et al. identify and estimate a proximal synthetic-control ATT with donor and supplemental-proxy roles fixed before estimation. Lee et al. condition on Gaussian polyhedra to obtain exact selective pivots, while Leeb, Pötscher, and Ewald calculate coverage for Gaussian post-model-selection intervals. Azzalini and Regoli establish even-functional invariance for skew-symmetric laws. None of these sources states the unconditional conventional-Wald coverage function for a statistic that switches between two proximal-ATT coordinates, its all-gap squared-correlation frontier, or a primitive proximal realization.
literature_map.correction_thread: Lunde proves that a separated future block is asymptotically independent of time-series model selection under beta mixing, and Andrews gives kernel HAC consistency and bandwidth analysis. These are method ancestors for the corrected estimator, not novelty targets. The open step is their uniform composition with proximal bridge estimation and scalar studentization when the full joint Gaussian covariance is singular.
literature_map.proximal_adjacent_threads: Section 5, Theorem 3 of Qiu et al. provides asymptotic normality for its fixed-role doubly robust GMM estimator under correctness of at least one bridge model. Cui et al. provide fixed-proxy proximal influence functions and efficiency bounds. Rakshit et al. select invalid proxies in an independent point-treatment model. These results confirm that role validity, role efficiency, and role selection are distinct from the present same-pre-period loss-selection coverage problem.

binary_wald_candidate.settled: Polyhedral conditioning, even-functional skew symmetry, fixed-role proximal linearization, and comparator-specific Gaussian coverage integration are settled.
binary_wald_candidate.exact_pair_check: No checked paper studies unconditional conventional symmetric-Wald coverage for a proximal ATT coordinate selected by a one-sided ridge-loss comparison.
binary_wald_candidate.closer_subsumption_check: Leeb, Pötscher, and Ewald is the closest coverage paper, but its nested-model preliminary-test statistic does not imply the two-role squared-correlation if-and-only-if condition or primitive proximal realizability.

singular_split_candidate.settled: Separated-block beta-mixing transfer, Bartlett-HAC consistency, and fixed-role proximal GMM expansions are settled separately.
singular_split_candidate.exact_pair_check: No checked theorem composes those pieces uniformly through a discontinuous finite selector when the stacked covariance can be singular.
singular_split_candidate.closer_subsumption_check: Lunde subsumes generic separation and therefore forces this candidate to locate novelty only in the uniform proximal inverse, fitted-score HAC, and singular selected-studentization map.

multi_role_candidate.settled: PoSI gives conservative simultaneous protection and Gaussian polyhedral conditioning gives conditional pivots for multiple selection regions.
multi_role_candidate.exact_pair_check: No checked paper gives an if-and-only-if covariance geometry for nominal unadjusted coverage over every local loss-gap vector in a multi-role proximal panel.
multi_role_candidate.closer_subsumption_check: PoSI does not subsume the exactness frontier, but the absence of a verified multivariate analogue of the binary squared-correlation condition leaves this candidate less feasible than the chosen kernel.

literature_map.bounded_search_result: Focused searches through September 13, 2026 found no paper combining pre-period donor--proxy role selection, a local ridge-loss tie, unconditional conventional symmetric-Wald coverage, and an if-and-only-if squared-correlation condition. This is a bounded literature conclusion rather than proof of absence.

novelty_justification: The closest causal comparator is Shi et al. (2026), whose Assumption 4 and Theorems 2--3 fix the donor/proxy partition before the proximal moment and HAC law. The closest inferential comparator is Leeb, Pötscher, and Ewald (2015), whose Proposition 3.1 gives Gaussian coverage formulas for a preliminary-test selector between nested regression models. The proposed strict delta is an estimator-specific theorem for a different object: a conventional symmetric interval centered at whichever of two correlated proximal-ATT statistics is chosen by a one-sided ridge-loss contrast. It supplies the exact function \(C_z(k)\), proves nominality for every local gap if and only if \(\rho_1^2=\rho_2^2\), gives the strict sign of the coverage error otherwise, and maps both regimes to an open family of primitive legal proximal panels. Lee et al., Azzalini--Regoli, Lunde, and Andrews are explicitly treated as technique sources rather than results being sharpened.
